hugely expansive, customisable, and packed with personality-- dst is a great experience that can keep you up for hours. there is so, so, so much content, enough that it can feel a little daunting at times. survival is mostly intuitive, although delving deeper requires, at times, a little bit of guesswork and bravery. 

the most defining aspect of dst is certainly its characters-- it's not a new feature in survival horrors, but i find that dst does an excellent job of making character choice feel important and game-changing, whilst still being balanced. additionally, the personality shines through in tons of small ways that add life to the game; dst goes to great lengths to make character choice feel weighty and meaningful rather than superfluous, and it really adds to the experience. 

that being said, the learning curve is fucking [i]steep[/i]. you will, in all likelihood, spend a frustrating amount of time dead or close. other survival games like minecraft, subnautica, and raft, usually only require 1-2 hours of gameplay before it stabilises, and your objectives shift to progression, rather than survival. dst is nothing like that. i found myself grappling with sanity, hunger, and health even 6 hours into a single game. personally, i found the challenge to be both frustrating and immersive-- whether you'll enjoy it is a matter of personal reflection. it's easier with friends, but can still be demoralising to watch a whole two hours of progress go up in flames.

dst is ultimately a punishing survival game with touches of horror and an excellent depth to it, made infinitely better with friends. pick webber he's quite literally the best!

I've played this game with a lot of different people and everyone quit before hitting 15 hours or so. We were always stuck doing endless chores at base and waiting for the night to end next to campfire. Eventually it was too boring to continue and that was it. 

But it's actually engaging once you are willing to learn the game and try to beat every boss. I did solo boss rush for the first time and it was fun af, even ended up making a good base (which probably took more in game days than it took me to get to Ancient Fuelweaver). Just the amount of things you need to learn and do to get to Celestial Champion is enough to discourage the most from continuing (especially Pearl's ridiculous quests). With that being said, it's not as complicated as one may think.

You can also download mods that make the game less frustrating and improve qol, such as: no thermal stone durability, minimap, combined status, boss health bar and etc, whatever suits you but wouldn't recommend going beyond that. 

Yes, good game.
